case: A founder reads that Kenya raised almost USD 1bn, then sees a sharp half-year decline. The decision depends on what each total actually counts.
caseLabel: Research cutoff 24 September 2026 • provider statistics and unverified screenshot claims stay separate
units: Amount — source-defined funding total; USD million
Venture count — distinct recipients above a stated threshold
Deal count — financing events, not necessarily unique companies
Release date — publication date, distinct from the transaction cutoff

beats.title: Dollars and breadth can move in opposite directions
points: ATBD’s primary 2025 post says Kenya raised almost USD 1bn.
It reports 75 ventures above USD 100,000, down 23% year on year.
A larger total can coexist with fewer qualifying recipients; neither measures application success.
beats.notes: Part 1, source [2]. The exact USD 984m is attributed in contemporary secondary coverage and the screenshot; do not present it as the precise wording of ATBD’s primary public post.

beats.title: Two providers define two measurement systems
points: ATBD: reported debt USD 582m and equity USD 383m.
Partech: rounded total USD 1.04bn; equity USD 539m and debt USD 498m.
The providers differ in thresholds, universe and count units. Do not average their totals.
beats.notes: Provider Comparison C5:L26 and Appendix 04. Headline spread is USD 56m, equity difference +USD 156m, debt difference −USD 84m. The category sums leave different residuals.

beats.title: Publication dates do not reveal data cutoffs
points: ATBD’s release: 13 January 2026; Partech’s release: 22 January 2026.
The nine-day publication gap does not prove a nine-day transaction cutoff gap.
Save provider, activity period, threshold, instrument scope, geography and date-assignment rule.
beats.notes: Reporting Vectors C5:F30. Neither public report establishes the transaction cutoff or event-date assignment rule. Mark those coordinates as unknown instead of inferring them.

calculation.title: Keep the unreconciled remainder visible
calculation.equation: Unassigned remainder = reported total − debt − equity
calculation.interpretation: The USD 19m difference is unassigned. The source summary does not establish that it is grants, rounding or another instrument.
calculation.notes: Funding Mix C5:F12, Market Metrics C5:G10 and Appendix 04. Partech’s rounded residual is approximately USD 3m: 1,040 − 539 − 498. Do not combine different dataset versions as an exact ledger.

scenario.title: Compare the same half-year in the same series
scenario.consequence: (126 ÷ 227) − 1 = −44.5%. This is a change in the tracker’s covered total, not a universal measure of confidence or access.
scenario.notes: Market Metrics C11:G16. Discuss Spiro’s geographic tagging as a coverage issue; do not assign pan-African cash to Kenya without the provider rule. The selected thirteen-company screenshot list totals KES 93.31bn; its KES 75.7bn top five yield 81.1%, a different denominator from national funding.

answer: A funding headline needs its amount, recipient count and coverage rules. Kenya’s large 2025 total and narrower qualifying-venture count answer different questions; unreconciled residuals and unknown cutoff rules must remain visible.
action: Save a one-page provider comparison with matched periods, thresholds, instruments, count units and unresolved coordinates before repeating a headline.

case: A business compares a debt facility and an equity offer by following who receives cash, what claim is created and what the downside requires.
caseLabel: Fictional financing scenarios • KES million unless stated • no lender offer implied
units: CFADS — cash flow available for debt service; KES/month
DSCR — CFADS ÷ scheduled principal and interest
Equal principal — the same principal amount repaid each month
Pre-money — equity value before the new investment
Post-money — pre-money value plus new primary investment

beats.title: The instrument determines the obligation
points: Equity creates an ownership claim; debt creates dated repayment obligations.
Leases, receivables finance and supplier credit fund different assets or cash gaps.
A SAFE or convertible adds conversion terms; a grant can add restrictions and milestones.
beats.notes: Instrument Guide C5:F14 and Appendix 02. Explain recipient, instrument, maturity, security, conversion and control separately rather than treating all funding headlines as the same capital.

beats.title: Follow the cash recipient
points: A primary investment can bring cash into the issuing company.
A secondary share sale may pay the existing shareholder instead.
Announcement, signing, close, draw and receipt are distinct states; a facility is not automatically cash on the bank statement.
beats.notes: Part 2 instrument and contract discussion. Preserve the legal issuer and recipient, currency, conditions precedent, draw status and cash evidence.

beats.title: Ownership percentage is a separate calculation
points: New primary investment: KES 30m at KES 120m pre-money.
Post-money equity value is KES 150m.
Simple new-investor ownership is 30 ÷ 150 = 20%, before additional option-pool or instrument adjustments.
beats.notes: Equity Dilution C5:K7. These are teaching assumptions. A cap table, liquidation preference, conversion and option pool can change the economic claim; simple ownership percentage is not a measure of cash repayment capacity.

calculation.title: Can month-one cash cover the debt schedule?
calculation.interpretation: Month-one principal is KES 4.167m and interest KES 1.5m: debt service is about KES 5.667m, leaving little operating cushion.
calculation.notes: Debt Service C5:M16 and full schedule to row 38. Hypothetical KES 100m facility, 24 equal-principal monthly payments, annual rate 18%; no unmodeled lender fees or grace periods are inferred.

scenario.title: Cash and interest can deteriorate together
scenario.baseline: CFADS KES 6.2m; 18% annual interest; DSCR about 1.09.
scenario.changed: CFADS falls 20% to KES 4.96m; annual interest rises to 23%.
scenario.consequence: Month-one debt service becomes about KES 6.083m; DSCR falls to about 0.82, with a cash shortfall of about KES 1.123m.
scenario.notes: Debt Service C5:M16. This is a specified two-input stress, not a forecast for any startup. Identify operating actions or explicit contract revisions that could close the gap; do not silently assume refinancing.

answer: Funding quality depends on fit between the use of cash and the instrument’s obligations. The fictional debt facility barely covers its first payment in the base case and fails coverage in the specified downside; the equity offer instead changes ownership and control.
action: Prepare a term-sheet record with issuer, recipient, amount, currency, draw conditions, fees, maturity, security, conversion and downside cash dates.

case: A reader follows thirteen company funding claims toward cash receipts, legal status and investor outcomes, leaving unresolved evidence visibly open.
caseLabel: Dated public evidence • cutoff 24 September 2026 • screenshot amounts remain claims until verified
units: Funding claim — stated amount before transaction-level verification
Legal recipient — exact entity receiving the financing
Recovery — evidenced distributions to a specific claim class
Status date — date at which the legal or operating state is established
Unknown — missing evidence; never substitute zero

beats.title: Four records must stay distinct
points: A company brand is not always the legal financing recipient.
A financing announcement is not proof of cash received.
An administration event does not, by itself, quantify an investor’s realized loss.
beats.notes: Part 3 and Appendix 03. Build separate company/entity, financing event, cash-receipt and current status fields. A published funding aggregate is not a balance sheet.

beats.title: Selected-list arithmetic is not deal verification
points: The screenshot’s thirteen claimed amounts sum to KES 93.31bn.
Its five largest claims sum to KES 75.7bn.
That selected-list ratio does not establish Kenya-wide concentration, domestic cash receipts or thirteen business failures.
beats.notes: Screenshot List C5:F21 and Appendix 01. Keep currency, event dates, instruments and recipients unverified until supported by transaction-level evidence.

beats.title: Keep legal entities and evidence status explicit
points: Twiga’s GT Flow and Templar Field records concern distinct legal entities.
For Copia, distinguish the Gazette appointment from a separately dated extension record.
A secondary report of administration is different evidence from an obtained primary notice.
beats.notes: Project 3 Case Register and Timeline; startup Appendix 03. Twiga’s USD 185.4m secondary-source funding aggregate does not establish cash received, runway or investor loss; legal recipient allocation remains unclear.

calculation.title: Use the denominator that the claim actually supports
calculation.equation: Selected-list top-five share = top-five claims ÷ all listed claims
calculation.interpretation: This reproduces the arithmetic of the selected thirteen-company screenshot. It does not validate any individual claim or measure the national market.
calculation.notes: Screenshot List C5:F21. The screenshot’s 82% claim and this 81.1% list calculation use different definitions from a verified same-version Kenya transaction ledger.

scenario.title: New evidence changes status, not unknown cash by assumption
scenario.baseline: The ledger contains a financing headline and an unresolved recipient or receipt amount.
scenario.changed: Obtain an entity-specific primary legal notice or transaction document.
scenario.consequence: Update only what that document establishes. Cash received and investor recovery remain unknown unless separate evidence reconciles them.
scenario.notes: This is an evidence-state comparison, not a numerical cash forecast. Track publication date, event date, document type and whether text is a party assertion, procedural order or court finding.

answer: The public record can establish particular financing statements and dated legal events. Investor loss requires a separate reconciliation of ownership, claim priority and actual recovery; missing coordinates should remain unknown.
action: Complete five passes: confirm the legal entity, verify each transaction, reconcile cash received, establish dated status and calculate recovery only from evidenced distributions.
